note: Colorbox Load has no config object, no permissions, no plugins and no Drush commands of its own. It registers one service (colorbox_load.renderer) tagged render.main_content_renderer with format 'drupal_colorbox' and attribute 'ng_lightbox: Colorbox', which adds a 'Colorbox' option to NG Lightbox's Renderer select. All configuration therefore lives in the ng_lightbox.settings config object (patterns, renderer, default_width, lightbox_class, skip_admin_paths) -- colorbox_load.info.yml literally declares 'configure: ng_lightbox.settings'. colorbox_load_install() writes renderer=drupal_colorbox. At runtime NG Lightbox rewrites matching links with use-ajax + data-dialog-type=colorbox, Drupal\colorbox_load\Renderer returns an AjaxResponse with a colorboxLoadOpen command, and js/colorbox_load.js opens $.colorbox() with the returned HTML. All medium/hard cases are grounded in that real ng_lightbox.settings state.

evals.prompt: The Drupal contrib module colorbox_load plugs into ng_lightbox so that page links open in a Colorbox overlay. What does it actually register with the service container to make 'Colorbox' show up as a choice in NG Lightbox's Renderer select, and what is the renderer/format id?
evals.expected_output: It defines the service colorbox_load.renderer (Drupal\colorbox_load\Renderer) tagged { name: render.main_content_renderer, format: drupal_colorbox, ng_lightbox: Colorbox }. The extra ng_lightbox attribute is collected by NG Lightbox's compiler pass into the ng_lightbox_renderers parameter, so 'Colorbox' appears in the Renderer select; the format/renderer id is drupal_colorbox.

evals.prompt: I installed colorbox_load on Drupal 11 but I can't find a settings page called 'Colorbox Load'. Which configuration object and admin path control which links open in the Colorbox lightbox, and which key lists the paths?
evals.expected_output: colorbox_load has no config of its own: its info.yml sets configure: ng_lightbox.settings, i.e. /admin/config/media/ng-lightbox. The config object is ng_lightbox.settings and the newline-separated list of leading-slash path patterns (wildcard *) is the 'patterns' key. Other keys: renderer, default_width, lightbox_class, skip_admin_paths.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal colorbox_load module, what happens between clicking a lightboxed link and the Colorbox appearing? Name the AJAX command the module defines and the JavaScript function that implements it.
evals.expected_output: Drupal\colorbox_load\Renderer::renderResponse() renders the main content with renderInIsolation() and returns an AjaxResponse containing Drupal\colorbox_load\OpenCommand, whose render() emits ['command' => 'colorboxLoadOpen', 'data' => $html]. js/colorbox_load.js implements Drupal.AjaxCommands.prototype.colorboxLoadOpen, which calls $.colorbox() with that HTML at 90% x 90% and re-runs Drupal.attachBehaviors().

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has colorbox_load enabled. Inspect the live configuration and tell me exactly which path patterns are currently configured to open in a lightbox, and which renderer is selected.
evals.expected_output: ng_lightbox.settings:patterns is "/cbl-demo/*\n/cbl-demo-two" and ng_lightbox.settings:renderer is drupal_colorbox (the renderer contributed by colorbox_load). Read it with: drush cget ng_lightbox.settings

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the Colorbox lightbox opened by colorbox_load has been given a custom CSS class, a non-default width, and admin pages are no longer excluded. Inspect the running site and report the CSS class value that is configured.
evals.expected_output: ng_lightbox.settings:lightbox_class is 'cbl-eval-overlay' (with default_width 845 and skip_admin_paths false). Read it with: drush cget ng_lightbox.settings

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, colorbox_load, colorbox and ng_lightbox are all enabled but nothing is being lightboxed. Configure the live site so that every link whose path starts with /cbl-task/ opens in a Colorbox overlay served by colorbox_load (not the core modal). Apply the change to the running site.
evals.expected_output: Set ng_lightbox.settings:renderer to drupal_colorbox and add a pattern line such as /cbl-task/* to ng_lightbox.settings:patterns, e.g. drush php:eval '\Drupal::configFactory()->getEditable("ng_lightbox.settings")->set("patterns", "/cbl-task/*")->set("renderer", "drupal_colorbox")->save();' (or via /admin/config/media/ng-lightbox).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the pop-up overlays produced by colorbox_load need restyling: they should carry the CSS class cbl-wide, use a default width of 960, and they must also be allowed to appear on administration pages. Keep Colorbox as the thing that renders them. Make the change on the live site.
evals.expected_output: In ng_lightbox.settings set lightbox_class: 'cbl-wide', default_width: 960, skip_admin_paths: false, renderer: 'drupal_colorbox' -- e.g. drush cset ng_lightbox.settings lightbox_class cbl-wide -y; drush cset ng_lightbox.settings default_width 960 -y; drush cset ng_lightbox.settings skip_admin_paths 0 -y.
